reason: Service-linked roles are created and owned by an AWS service, not by us. They are 49 of 152 roles here and their permissions are fixed by AWS, so they add volume without adding anything we can change. Roles at /service-role/ are NOT dropped - those were created for our resources and are ours.
Belt and braces alongside Owners=self: a public AMI is not an asset of this account even if the owner filter is ever relaxed.
Amazon-owned snapshots are catalogue entries rather than our data.

A terminated instance is not part of the estate. AWS keeps returning it from DescribeInstances for up to an hour and strips its SubnetId, so it can never be placed in the network it used to occupy - it drew as a workload floating loose in the availability zone. 12 of this account's 17 instances were terminated.
A closed spot request bought nothing that still exists. Same failure mode as a terminated instance: it has no network placement and stacks up in the zone box.

DescribeVpcEndpointServices returns every service offering PrivateLink in the region, not the ones we own - 348 of 348 here are Owner=amazon, AWS's own catalog. It has no API parameter to ask for ours only. What we own is a VPC endpoint SERVICE we published; those carry the account id as Owner and are kept.
